   STAFF REPORT
 Meeting Date:  December 17, 2024
 To:  Arts and Culture Council Liaisons Councilmember John Mirisch and
  Councilmember Mary Wells
 From:  Matthew Brown, Recreation Services Manager
  Corrina Lesser, Recreation Supervisor
 Subject:  Interactive Kiosks Program
 Attachments:  None

INTRODUCTION
The City of Beverly Hills is a local, regional, and international destination. As Los Angeles
County prepares to host several major sporting events that draw significant global interest,
including the FIFA World Cup in 2026, the Super Bowl in 2027, and the Olympic and
Paralympic Games in 2028, Beverly Hills will continue to play host to a significant number
of visitors from all over the world.

In anticipation of these large-scale, regional and international events, and a desire to
connect visitors to the City’s dynamic cultural treasures – both past and present – the Arts
and Culture Commission identified a proposed interactive visitor digital kiosk program as
a Commission priority in both its 2023 and 2024 priority-setting exercises. Having an
interactive kiosk program would have the potential to allow visitors to access the City’s
rich array of arts and culture opportunities, events, and programs of interest, and learn
about the City’s unique history.

The Commission and Community Services Staff understand that a digital kiosk program
proposal has previously been considered by the City, and thus far has not been supported.
A brief timeline and synopsis of previous opportunities to review a kiosk program,
occurring between December 2017 and September 2024, are summarized as follows:
2017
On December 20, 2017, Orange Barrel Media/IKE Smart City met with the Chamber of
Commerce Liaisons about its digital kiosk program, which was to be funded using a
 Meeting Date: December 17, 2024

digital advertising model. Following the presentation, the company was invited to return to
the committee at a future meeting, and prepare a presentation focused on smaller-sized
kiosks.
2018
On March 1, 2018, Orange Barrel Media/IKE Smart City returned to the Chamber of
Commerce Liaison Committee to present the smaller-format interactive kiosks as
requested, along with information detailing some proposed kiosk locations, and updated
kiosk dimensions. At the conclusion of that meeting, it was requested that the vendor
prepare a presentation featuring an even smaller kiosk, and again return to the Committee
at a future meeting with a new presentation.
2019
On January 11, 2019, the vendor returned with a presentation, and revealed the new “IKE
Super Mini” kiosk, that would be the first-of-its-kind kiosk. Proposed locations were
provided to the Committee. It was also noted that the agreement for the kiosks would be
forged between the vendor and the Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce, with a
percentage revenue share with the Chamber based upon digital advertisement revenue.
The vendor would have also been required to obtain an encroachment permit from the
City, along with a business tax certificate, both of which would have been paid on an
annual basis to the City. Direction from the Committee at the time, was that additional
Liaison meetings to review the proposal were not needed, and that prior to further
consideration, additional information would need to be vetted, with any continuing
discussions at the City Council study session level. Some of the additional information
sought, included identifying public benefits from the kiosks, having discussions with
business and property owners located near the proposed kiosk locations, and reviewing
potential contract and permit terms. Ultimately, the proposal did not move forward for
further consideration beyond the Committee, prior to the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic,
at which time priorities shifted to other areas.
2024
On September 2, 2024, the Beverly Hills City Council Liaison/Small Business Assistance
Task Force Committee convened for their September meeting. During this meeting, City
staff, business owners from the South Beverly Merchants Association, and
representatives from the Chamber of Commerce, discussed some of the City’s prior
reviews of digital kiosk programs – including the analysis that kiosk installation and
maintenance would be prohibitively expensive (particularly in light of upcoming projected
budget deficits), given that existing business models for kiosks rely on advertising
revenue, and Beverly Hills has not been inclined to allow the kiosks to function as mini
billboards or advertising space for marketing campaigns.
The Committee also expressed concerns that other applications currently exist to guide
or inform visitors about local events or areas of interest in Beverly Hills, which the City
already supports in some way. The Conference and Visitors’ Bureau (CVB) currently has
2 apps aimed at tourists to promote business; Love Beverly Hills is run by the CVB and is
for restaurant, hotel, and event promotion; and the Historical Society provides walking
tours of the City. More collaboration between these entities, and local merchants, was
encouraged to take full advantage of the existing applications.
On November 19, 2024, the City announced that a public safety center would be
constructed at the planned Wilshire/La Cienega Metro station in Beverly Hills, which could
also serve as another means of disseminating information to visitors.

Page 2 of 3
 Meeting Date: December 17, 2024

DISCUSSION
With the opportunity for an interactive kiosk program to showcase the community’s artistic
and cultural assets, and major sporting events bringing global visitors to Los Angeles from
all over the world, the Arts and Culture Commission is seeking opportunities to re-engage
consideration of an interactive kiosk program.
Local municipalities including Santa Monica and Culver City have adopted digital kiosk
programs to enhance resident and visitor experiences, as well as generate revenue for
the respective municipalities. To adopt a kiosk program with the ability to bring in more
lucrative advertising revenue, Culver City amended ordinance language limiting national
advertising, while both Culver City and Santa Monica employ similarly restrictive
advertising criteria and include means of highlighting local businesses.
With the continuing adoption of this technology regionally, the Arts and Culture
Commission has identified a digital kiosk program as a priority by adding it to their work
plan and views the current time as opportune to reconsider interactive kiosks, ahead of
upcoming events in Los Angeles.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact at this time. If the item is supported staff will return with potential
costs or revenues associated with the program.

RECOMMENDATION
The Arts and Culture Commission is seeking support and/or direction from the Arts and
Culture Council Liaisons on a digital interactive kiosk program.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Service
  Approved By

   STAFF REPORT
 Meeting Date:  December 17, 2024
 To:  Arts and Culture Council Liaisons Councilmember John Mirisch and
  Councilmember Mary Wells
 From:  Matthew Brown, Recreation Services Manager
  Sara Scrimshaw, Venue Supervisor – Historic Site
 Subject:  Beverly Hills International Music Festival co-sponsorship request to use
  the Greystone Mansion

 Attachments:  None

INTRODUCTION
As has been requested in prior years, Beverly Hills International Music Festival (BHIMF)
has requested the City’s co-sponsorship, and use of the Greystone Mansion, for the return
of the Beverly Hills International Music Festival in the spring of 2025. Founded in 2004,
BHIMF is a non-profit organization that aims to bring classical and jazz music, performed
by local and internationally acclaimed musicians, to Beverly Hills and the region, to
promote excellence in performance and musical education. BHIMF was last held at the
Greystone Mansion in 2019 for what at the time was the 16th annual festival - and seeks
to return the festival to Greystone with performances in 2025. As part of returning the
festival to Greystone Mansion in 2025, two concert dates can be accommodated at
Greystone, likely in the spring of 2025. Finalized concert dates will be confirmed as soon
as possible, in continuing discussions between BHIMF and Community Services staff.

DISCUSSION
Like prior years, to produce the concert performances, BHIMF is requesting in-kind
services from the City of Beverly Hills, to offset the cost of Greystone facility rental fees.
To facilitate the events, Greystone staff would provide day-of event support, including the
set-up and break-down of Greystone chairs for the concerts. If a piano is needed for any
of the concert performances, BHIMF would be responsible for supplying the piano, and
 Meeting Date: December 17, 2024

coordinating any delivery and removal logistics before and after the concerts, with
Community Services staff.
BHIMF will be charging for tickets, as has been done in prior years, with a percentage of
tickets to be offered to Beverly Hills residents free of charge. Revenue from ticket sales,
could help offset BHIMF operating costs. As planning for the concerts is still ongoing, exact
ticket prices, allocated number of tickets for Beverly Hills residents, and total number of
tickets available for sale, is still to be finalized. Greystone can accommodate up to 70
people for each performance.

FISCAL IMPACT
In calculating the anticipated fees that would be waived for the performances, Community
Services staff project costs of approximately $1,300 in Ranger and Greystone staff time
for set-up and break-down, and approximately $3,190 in rental fees for use of space at
Greystone for the concerts, for a total of $4,490 that would be waived to produce the
concerts.

RECOMMENDATION
Following past practice and direction from City Council in prior years, Community Services
staff recommends that the Arts and Culture Council Liaisons, support the City’s co-
sponsorship of the BHIMF performances, and the waiver of associated staff time and
Greystone rental use costs to produce the concerts.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Service
  Approved By
